full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary for the purpose of disposal of this Rule are that the petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 195 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka praying a decree declaring that the plaintiff is entitled to get an amount of Taka 1,01,77,175.40 (Taka one crore one lakh seventy seven thousand one hundred seventy five and paisa forty) with compensation at the bank rate of 16% till realization of the amount of Taka 1,0177,175.40. The plaintiffs case, in brief, is that the plaintiff is a member of legal profession in Bangladesh and is being enrolled as an Advocate on 3-2-1979 and became member of Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar since 1989 and has been rendering legal services towards his clients efficiently, diligently, honestly and without an iota of any grievances from any quarter since long 25 years of the length of his profession. The plaintiff is the Legal Adviser and Law consultant of local and foreign companies and firms and he is associated with many national and international organizations and internationally reputed person and that he earned good name and fame in Bangladesh and in abroad. The defendant Nod Bank is a Banking Institution established under Bank companies Act and the defendant Nos. 9-14 are the branch in charge and the defendant Nos. 2-8 are the executives of the Bank and all their acts, subject to laws shall be the acts of the defendant No.1 and in case of misuse of power they shall be liable personally. The defendant No.1 considering the worthiness, efficiency and good will appointed the plaintiff as their panel lawyer of the Bank vide appointment letter No. HO/CD/LAWYER/91/1528/1372 dated 31-8-1991 enclosing the prescribed schedule of fees of Bank's circular No.468 dated 19-2-1991 for conducting legal matters, suits and appeal in the Judge's court as well as in the High Court Division in its original, appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. The plaintiff appeared in and conducted several cases on behalf of the defendant Bank since 31-8-1991 as Panel Lawyer and legal adviser on approved rate of the case for appearing and conducting suits and cases till disposal, and for other legal matters. The defendant No. 9 vide their letter No. UBL/LO/SD/2005 /33 dated 19-1-2005 instructed the plaintiff to file both Title Suit and Criminal case against M/s Southern Beverage Industries Ltd. (CC A/C No. 557) for realization of bank's dues. The assignment was given to the plaintiff offering special fees beyond the prescribed rate of fees provided in circular No. 468 dated 19-2-1991. The defendant No. 9 Paid Taka 10,000 as advance to the plaintiff vide payment order dated 27-1-2005 and thereafter the plaintiff prepared the plaint and sent the same to the bank for verification of facts along with a bill dated 29-1-2005 for Taka 1,01,000 and it was received by the bank on 1-2-2005 under their seal and signature, subsequently the plaint was not returned to the plaintiff for filing in court and contractual fees was not paid even demands made by the plaintiff. The withholding of the plaintiffs long outstanding bills without assigning any reason whatsoever has caused heavy loss and damages, injury to the plaintiff. 

 3. While on 21-4-2011 the case was fixed for service of summons as well as taking steps and on that fixed date the plaintiff-petitioner filed an application for time. 

 4. The trial Court by its order dated 21-4-2011 dismissed the case for default. 

 6. The learned Judge of the trial Court after hearing rejected the application by his order dated 25-7-2012 on the finding that the application filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the dismissal order for default is misconceived and not tenable in law. 

 8. Mr NAM Abdur Razzaque, Advocate in person appears before this court and contends that the learned Joint District Judge seriously erred in law in rejecting the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the dismissal order for default dated 21-4-2011 without properly considering the facts of the case and the case made out by the petitioner and the same has occasioned failure of justice. Finally, Mr Abdur Razzaque submits that if the dismissal order for default is set-aside in that event he will pay an amount of Taka 5,000 as cost in favour of the opposite party, Bank. 

 11. It appears that on the date fixed for service of summons as well as taking steps the petitioner filed an application for time. The learned Joint District Judge by its order dated 21-4-2011 after rejecting the application for time dismissed the case for default stating as follows: অদ্য বিবাদীর প্রতি সমনজারী বিষয়ে তদ্বীর গ্রহনের জন্য ধার্য্য আছে। বাদী দরখাস্ত দিয়া সময়ের প্রার্থনা করেন। ডাক মতে বাদী অনুপস্থিত । সময়ের দরখাস্ত না মনজুর করা হইল । (VOP) এখন সময় ৪-২৫। বার বার উচ্চ ম্বরে ডাকা স্বত্বেও বাদীপক্ষ বা নিযুক্তিয় আইনজীবিকে পাওয়া গেল না। মোকদ্দমাটি খারিজ এর সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহিত হইল। The petitioner, thereafter, on 22-5-2011 filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the dismissal order for default dated 21-4-2011. 

 12. In the instant case the petitioner him-self as an Advocate having knowledge of the limitation although the reasons best known to him as to why without sufficient cause slept over the matter over a period of one month and then filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the default order without availing the alternative remedy is open to him. 

 13. The trial Court in its discretion rejected the application inasmuch as the application was not filed according to the provisions of law. In the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject, we do not think that the trial judge committed any illegality in rejecting the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the dismissal order for default. 

 14. Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure simply confirms the Courts inherent power and this power cannot be exercised where alternative remedies by way of appeal, revision or review are available. An application under section 151 CPC in such a case is not maintainable. Therefore, we do not find any possible reason to differ with the view taken by the trial Court below. 

 15. Moreover, on going through the con-tents of the plaint together with the conduct of the plaintiff- Advocate in this case since 2005 to till today, we are not at all inclined to give him a chance to proceed with the matter further whatsoever. In the facts of the present case, we are constrained to observe that it is also a part of professional misconduct if an Advocate in order to get undue benefit filed a case against his client claiming huge amount as fees and deliberately hanged case years together. This Court discourages this type of conduct of an Advocate of this court. 

 16. In this case the learned Joint District Judge clearly found that the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the dismissal order default was not tenable in law and rejected the same on sound and good reasons. We are satisfied that the learned Joint District Judge duly applied his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the law bearing on the subject and passed the impugned order on sound reasons. The impugned order is found to be well-reasoned and well-supported by both law and facts. We, therefore, do not find any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned order occasioning failure of justice so as to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
